records.issue_text: The prisma.workflowReminder.update inside the catch block (scheduleSMSReminders.ts:178-186/188-196) is unguarded, so a failure of that update (e.g., P2025 if the row was deleted) throws out of the catch handler, skipping remaining reminders and returning a 500
records.rationale: In the new catch block, the code does `await prisma.workflowReminder.update({ where: { id: reminder.id }, data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 } })` without wrapping that update in its own try/catch. If that update throws (e.g., Prisma P2025 if the row no longer exists due to concurrent deletion/processing), the exception will escape the catch handler and abort the loop/handler, potentially yielding a 500 and skipping remaining reminders.

records.issue_text: A reminder that fails twice in the same run is never filtered out after incrementing, and the delete-purge only runs at the start of the next invocation, so there is no retry cap enforced within the sending loop and the reminder is re-attempted on every subsequent cron run
records.rationale: The diff *does* enforce a retry cap across cron invocations by purging reminders with `retryCount > 1` at the start of each run: `deleteMany({ where: { OR: [..., { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } ] } })`. Also, nothing in the shown loop attempts the same reminder twice “in the same run”; reminders are fetched once into `unscheduledReminders` and then processed once each, with at most a single `retryCount + 1` update on failure. Therefore the claim that it is “re-attempted on every subsequent cron run” is contradicted by the purge condition.

records.issue_text: retryCount increment is a non-atomic read-then-write, and overlapping cron invocations can halve the retry budget; should use prisma increment operator
records.rationale: The diff increments `retryCount` via a non-atomic read-then-write: `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` in both the `else` branch and the `catch` block. Since `reminder.retryCount` comes from a prior `findMany` select, concurrent/overlapping invocations can read the same value and both write back the same incremented value, losing an increment. Using Prisma’s atomic `{ increment: 1 }` would avoid this lost-update bug.

records.issue_text: retryCount is never reset to 0 on success, so a reminder that succeeds after failures still carries stale count and can be wrongly deleted on the next cron tick
records.rationale: The diff introduces deletion of any `WorkflowReminder` with `retryCount > 1` (`deleteMany` where `OR: [..., { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]`). The scheduling logic increments `retryCount` on failure paths (`else` and `catch` both `data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 }`) but on success it only updates `scheduledDate` and `referenceId` and never resets `retryCount` to 0. Therefore a reminder that eventually succeeds after 2+ failures will retain `retryCount > 1` and be eligible for deletion on the next cron run even if it’s now successfully scheduled.
